headline: 40,000 LEAFLETS PRINTED WITH THE WRONG CONSTITUENCY
body: The printers have delivered forty thousand glossy leaflets inviting the good people of 'Harwich and Stoke Minster' to vote for a candidate who 'knows this area like the back of her hand'. Harwich is 140 miles away.

responses.label: Reprint everything overnight
responses.flavour: The new leaflets arrive at dawn, still warm. Nobody ever knows. The treasurer knows.

responses.label: Deliver them and lean into the joke
responses.flavour: Priya records a video with a map and a sheepish grin. The graduates love it. The retirees write to the paper, on the back of the leaflet.

responses.label: Blame the printers in a press release
responses.hint: The printers also print the local paper.
responses.flavour: The printers respond with a scan of the order form, signed by your office, with 'Harwich' underlined twice.

headline: REGIONAL TV WANTS A HEAD-TO-HEAD DEBATE
body: Forty minutes, live, against an incumbent who has done this nine times and once made a presenter cry. The audience is 'balanced', which in Harwell means furious from several directions at once.

responses.label: Accept the debate
responses.flavour: You accept. The producers send over the format: four themes, one closing statement, and a studio audience member who has asked for 'a microphone, specifically'.

responses.label: Send a statement and an empty chair
responses.hint: The chair will be photographed. A lot.
responses.flavour: The empty chair trends by nine o'clock. By ten, someone has given it a name, a campaign slogan, and a higher approval rating than your candidate.

headline: ONE LINE THEY'LL REMEMBER. WHICH ONE?
body: Debates are won on clips. You have time to drill exactly one moment into her. Choose it well: whatever you pick, she will say it whether or not it fits.

responses.label: The bypass, costed to the penny
responses.flavour: She recites the bypass costings with total command. The incumbent looks rattled for the first time in a decade. The clip is two minutes long and nobody shares it.

responses.label: A zinger about the incumbent's second home
responses.flavour: 'He knows the M4 better than he knows Harwell.' It lands. It lands so hard that the incumbent's reply is drowned out by a man in the audience shouting 'the M4!' for the rest of the hour.

responses.label: A heartfelt story about her grandmother
responses.hint: It has to be true. Please let it be true.
responses.flavour: It is true, broadly. The grandmother, reached by a tabloid in Surrey, confirms 'most of it' and asks why nobody has visited.

headline: THE PARTY LEADER WANTS TO VISIT. TOMORROW.
body: Headquarters has pencilled in a leader's visit to a marginal seat, and yours is the marginal seat. The leader polls terribly locally, brilliantly nationally, and has asked to be photographed 'with a cow, ideally'.

responses.label: Roll out the red carpet (and the cow)
responses.hint: The cow has not been briefed.
responses.flavour: The visit is confirmed. A farm is found. A cow is found. The cow's owner asks, reasonably, who is paying for the cow.

responses.label: Politely suggest the leader is needed elsewhere
responses.flavour: Headquarters agrees, coolly. The leader visits the neighbouring seat instead and says something unflattering about bypasses that is quoted on every doorstep in Harwell.

responses.label: Leak that the leader is 'nervous about Harwell'
responses.hint: Underdog stories sell. So do knives.
responses.flavour: The leak runs as a front page: LEADER SWERVES MARGINAL. Priya becomes, overnight, the plucky local rebel. Headquarters becomes, overnight, very interested in who leaked it.

headline: LEADER MEETS COW
body: Six cameras. One cow. The leader approaches it with the confidence of someone who has seen a cow in a book. Priya is standing between them. Nobody has told her where to stand.

responses.label: Tell Priya to step back and let the leader own it
responses.hint: The leader's moment. The leader's risk.
responses.flavour: The leader pats the cow. The cow tolerates it. The photograph runs nationally with Priya's elbow just in shot, which the local paper crops to make it look deliberate.

responses.label: Tell Priya to take the cow's head
responses.hint: She has never touched a cow. It cannot be that hard.
responses.flavour: Priya takes hold of the cow with total, consultant-grade confidence. The cow, a veteran of three county shows, respects it. The photo becomes her campaign poster by lunchtime.

headline: EXCLUSIVE: CANDIDATE CLAIMED FOR 'FLOATING COFFEE STATION'
body: A national paper has Priya's old consultancy expenses. Among them: £4,300 for a 'floating coffee station' for an office pond. The pond, it turns out, was also expensed. So was the duck.

responses.label: Full apology and a donation to charity
responses.hint: Costs money. Costs dignity. Buys something.
responses.flavour: Priya apologises on the steps of the town hall and writes a cheque to the local wildfowl sanctuary. The sanctuary names a duck after her. It is a very unflattering duck.

responses.label: It was private-sector money. Next question.
responses.hint: Technically true. Technically is doing a lot of work.
responses.flavour: The line holds with the graduates, who assume everyone expenses a duck. The retirees do not assume that. The retirees have never expensed anything.

responses.label: Find something worse in the incumbent's past
responses.flavour: The incumbent, it emerges, once expensed a moat. Nobody talks about the coffee station again. Nobody talks about policy again either. Turnout forecasts dip across the board.
